# Optiq

> Optiq (npm package `optiq-image`) optimises images with verified quality. For every image it encodes a bounded set
> of candidates with WASM codecs (jpegli, libwebp, libavif, oxipng), measures each against the input, and returns
> the smallest output that meets the constraint: pixel-exact (`lossless`), SSIM >= 0.99 (`visually-lossless`),
> SSIM >= 0.975 (`balanced`, default) or `fast` (balanced threshold, no AVIF, <= 5 encodes). Runs in the browser
> (Web Worker) and in Node. Apache-2.0. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.

Key facts:
- Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF (static; animated kept as is). SVG is passed through unchanged. HEIC/HEIF is
  rejected with `UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT`.
- Formats are detected from content, not extensions. Transparency, EXIF orientation and ICC profiles are kept;
  JPEG is never chosen for images with alpha.
- Metadata (EXIF, XMP) is kept by default; `preserveMetadata: false` / `--strip-metadata` removes it, including GPS.
- SSIM is a proxy for perception, not a guarantee of invisible change. AVIF is held to a stricter SSIM threshold,
  calibrated against SSIMULACRA2. Outputs are also scored with SSIMULACRA2 in the benchmarks.
- Typical cost: 0.3-3 s per image (several encodes each); large screenshots in visually-lossless can take tens of
  seconds. Much slower than a single canvas encode.
- Lossy outputs written by the CLI/MCP server carry a ~20-byte marker; marked files are not re-encoded again
  (repeated lossy passes compound loss). `--reoptimize` overrides.

## For agents

- MCP server: `npx -y optiq-mcp` (stdio). Tools: `analyze_images` (read-only dry run) and `optimize_images`
  (`write: "in-place"` keeps formats and names; `write: "out-dir"` may change formats). Claude Code:
  `claude mcp add optiq -- npx -y optiq-mcp`.
- CLI: `npx -y optiq-image <files|folders> --json` is a dry run; add `--in-place` (keeps format, atomic, only if
  smaller) or `--out <dir>`. Options: `--mode`, `--formats webp,jpeg`, `--max-size <px>`, `--strip-metadata`,
  `--min-quality <ssim>`, `--min-saving <ratio>`, `--reoptimize`, `--concurrency <n>`. Exit 0 ok, 1 usage error,
  2 some files failed (others processed).
- Agent Skill: https://github.com/Baukaalm/optiq/blob/main/skills/optiq/SKILL.md

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://baukaalm.github.io/optiq/guide/getting-started): browser usage, `compressImage(file, options)`
- [Modes and quality](https://baukaalm.github.io/optiq/guide/modes)
- [Options and results](https://baukaalm.github.io/optiq/guide/options)
- [Formats, metadata, colour](https://baukaalm.github.io/optiq/guide/formats)
- [Errors](https://baukaalm.github.io/optiq/guide/errors): `OptiqError` codes
- [Bundlers](https://baukaalm.github.io/optiq/guide/bundlers): Vite, webpack, workers and WASM
- [Uploading to S3](https://baukaalm.github.io/optiq/guide/s3): `compressAndUpload` with presigned URLs
- [React hook](https://baukaalm.github.io/optiq/guide/react): `useOptiq` from `optiq-image/react`
- [CLI and Vite plugin](https://baukaalm.github.io/optiq/guide/static)
- [AI agents](https://baukaalm.github.io/optiq/guide/agents): MCP server, skill
- [Benchmarks](https://baukaalm.github.io/optiq/benchmarks): 24-image corpus. balanced -61% total with SSIMULACRA2
  median 79 (WebP q80: -51%, 79). visually-lossless -50% with median 86. Gradients are the weakest category.
